title: Questioning the problem-solving process
coreMove: Separate problem definition, diagnosis, and action, then structure the inquiry before trusting the recommendation.
sourcePressure: Chapter 8 moves upstream to problem solving: what the problem is, why it exists, what to do about it, period graph books, structuring analysis of the problem, and the logic-tree concept.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the visible symptom or preferred fix as the problem and then organizing a recommendation around that shortcut.
sourceAlignmentTerms: what should we do about it

sourceAnchors.name: logic tree
sourceAnchors.detail: the Chapter 8 sidecar states that the logic-tree concept appears as a structural aid inside the analytical process
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A logic tree earns its keep only when it opens the field of causes before one favorite explanation takes over.

sourceAnchors.name: What is the problem / why does it exist / what should we do about it
sourceAnchors.detail: the authorized heading map separates problem definition, causal analysis, and action choice
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Definition, diagnosis, and action are different jobs; when they blur, the outline starts carrying borrowed certainty.

hook: The meeting room waits while a slide tries to explain itself
opening with an abstract definition of clarity
starting with a generic frustrated professional staring at a blank document
counterintuition: Most people think formatting solves clarity; actually thinking solves clarity
clarity is not about writing less; it is about thinking better
structure sounds rigid but actually creates freedom

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective recognition, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm through a direct second-person passage, a short research/source aside, a reader question, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a public-transit planning unit investigating late evening buses
exampleSpecs.stakes: the city may add buses when the real issue is dispatch gaps or transfer timing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan writes late buses as a symptom, branches the issue into dispatch, traffic, and transfer timing, and refuses to recommend added service until each branch is tested.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A wall map shows red pins along three late-night routes.

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital cafeteria team analyzing uneaten patient meals
exampleSpecs.stakes: budget will be spent on new menus if timing, temperature, or dietary mismatches are not separated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Étienne asks whether taste is the problem, then builds branches for delivery timing, tray temperature, dietary fit, and menu choice before recommending anything.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Are patients rejecting the food, or is the food arriving too late to be food?

exampleSpecs.domain: a university lab investigating failed replication attempts
exampleSpecs.audience: research teams structuring inquiry before corrective action
exampleSpecs.stakes: months of work may be wasted if technique, reagent quality, and sample preparation are not diagnosed separately
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula labels the failure as the visible result, then builds a cause tree before choosing whether to retrain staff or replace reagents.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A tray of cloudy wells sits under the lab hood light.

exampleSpecs.domain: a bookshop owner tracing declining weekday sales
exampleSpecs.stakes: discounting will cut margin if the real cause is nearby construction or inventory mismatch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chris replaces the blunt problem sales are down with branches for foot traffic, conversion, and basket size, then tests each before choosing an action.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Chris three quiet Tuesdays to stop calling the symptom the problem.

exampleSpecs.domain: an emergency-management office reviewing slow storm-shelter openings
exampleSpecs.stakes: residents could wait outside shelters again if staffing, keys, and alert protocols remain one vague issue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 7:05 a.m., Marit refuses to write staff failed, divides the process into alert, access, staffing, and supply branches, and marks which branch lacks evidence.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 7:05 a.m., Marit pins a shelter-opening timeline beside the radio log.

exampleSpecs.domain: a game-studio producer diagnosing repeated build failures
exampleSpecs.audience: software production teams separating causes from fixes
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may buy tooling when build failures stem from asset handoff rules
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "The failed build is not the problem yet," Akira says, then draws branches for assets, code merges, tests, and release timing before assigning fixes.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "The failed build is not the problem yet," Akira says with the error log projected behind him.

skillTargets: hold action until diagnosis has been structured
use a logic tree to divide the field without overclaiming
identify when polished structure rests on weak inquiry

tryThisNowSpec: For one current issue, write three lines: symptom, possible causes, proposed action. If the first and third lines are the same, stop and define the problem again.
